ev.q: many of these children came from poor immigrant families and were being tested in a language they had only recently begun to learn

1.why: A段末句。a reason why early research results may have been misleading ↔ Later researchers … pointed out that many of these children came from poor immigrant families and were being tested in a language they had only recently begun to learn。F段也讲研究结果可能有偏差，但那是2000年代关于认知优势的研究，与“早期”不符，是近似干扰。

ev.q: compares this to a person with savings in two bank accounts

2.why: C段 Ellison。a comparison with the way money can be kept ↔ savings in two bank accounts。

ev.q: By around eight months, babies growing up with only one language have lost this ability

3.why: B段。an ability that monolingual babies lose ↔ babies growing up with only one language have lost this ability（通过面部动作分辨语言切换）。

ev.q: Children usually mix languages when they are speaking to someone who also understands both, and they tend to use only one language with people who do not

4.why: D段。choose a language for different listeners ↔ mix languages when speaking to someone who also understands both … only one language with people who do not。E段讲的是父母的语言策略，不是孩子自己的选择。

ev.q: studies which found an advantage were more likely to be published

5.why: F段 Brooks。more likely to appear in print ↔ more likely to be published。

ev.q: are much less likely to speak it, even if they understand it

6.why: E段。understanding a language that they do not speak ↔ much less likely to speak it, even if they understand it。

ev.q: notice when a speaker on a silent video switches from one language to another, simply by watching the movements of the speaker's face

7.why: B段。noticed a change of language without hearing it ↔ notice when a speaker on a silent video switches … simply by watching the movements of the speaker's face。D 是干扰：失去能力的是8个月大的单语婴儿，不是对脸失去兴趣；B、C 文中未提。

ev.q: looking at only one account gives a misleading impression of how much they have

8.why: C段。gives a false idea of how much the child knows ↔ gives a misleading impression of how much they have（类比：只看一个账户会低估总存款）。A 正是 Ellison 要反驳的误解；D 是A段中过去的建议。

ev.q: Adult bilinguals do exactly the same thing, and their switches follow grammatical rules rather than occurring at random

9.why: D段末句。Their changes of language follow grammatical patterns ↔ their switches follow grammatical rules rather than occurring at random。A、D 与 do exactly the same thing（和孩子一样会混用）相反；C 文中未提。

ev.q: the strategy itself matters less than the amount of contact the child has with each language

10.why: E段。how much the child hears each language ↔ the amount of contact the child has with each language。A（一人一语）和 B（家里说一种）都是被说成“没那么重要”的具体策略，正是本题的陷阱。

ev.q: hearing two languages would confuse young children, delay their speech and harm their progress at school

11.why: A段。feared ↔ worried；slow down ↔ delay；children's ___ ↔ their speech。progress 也在同句，但原文是 harm their progress，与 slow down 对应的是 delay their speech。

ev.q: Because bilinguals must constantly control which language they are using

12.why: F段。the constant need to ↔ must constantly；___ their choice of language ↔ control which language they are using。concentrating 是结果，不是需要做的动作。

ev.q: the ability to talk with grandparents and relatives

13.why: G段。communicating with ↔ the ability to talk with；other family members ↔ relatives（题干已改写），所以填 grandparents。
